title: The Next Game Engine Won't Have a Manual — Arturo Nunez, Nereu
talk_summary: A game-engine founder demos an AI assistant that edits a scene by applying predefined tags/systems rather than generating code, and explains how he builds the engine with an LLM. The transferable core is constraining the agent to a small vocabulary of pre-built operations plus LOD-style context assembly.

takeaways.technique: Constrain agent to a fixed tag/system vocabulary instead of free-form code
takeaways.what_they_do: The engine exposes only built-in tags and systems; the assistant's job is to add/remove tags on assets, not write scripts, so it cannot reinvent boilerplate.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent just performs calls and appends or removes the the tags. All these tags and all these systems are built into the the the the engine.

takeaways.what_they_do: Only the object being edited and its immediate neighbors get full tag/value detail; distant objects get a one-line summary or are dropped entirely.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if the user is editing the game ... the things that are around it might have a higher priority ... Things that are nearby, we just say, 'Okay, there's a something that's a player here'

takeaways.technique: Append domain/genre context to every prompt
takeaways.what_they_do: They append scene-derived context (asset types in use, the kind of game the user described) to the base prompt so the model's vocabulary matches the project.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We also allow the the user to describe the type of game that they want to to make. So, that's also part of what is is appended into the into the the context.

takeaways.technique: Auto-tag assets with a vision model offline
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of hand-labeling 6-7k 3D assets, they screenshot each and run a vision model to produce descriptions used for retrieval.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I took a screenshot and ran a a vision model to describe the those.

takeaways.technique: Feed tool definitions to the assistant as tools are built
takeaways.what_they_do: Whenever a new engine tool is added, its definition is handed to the assistant so it knows the available operations.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every time uh we add new tools, the assistant knows the the tools that we're we're adding
I don't think we need this setting. I don't think we need this feature. I haven't seen a lot of users using those things. So, let's get rid of them
